value: Up to 4 marks. Nirguna Brahman: formless, without qualities or attributes, beyond description — Taittiriya Upanishad 2.7.1-2 (1 mark). Saguna Brahman: Brahman with qualities, personal, able to be worshipped — Rig Veda 1.154 describes Vishnu as a Saguna form (1 mark). Practice: most Hindus approach Saguna Brahman through murti and the deities, while Nirguna Brahman is approached through meditation and study (1 mark).

value: Up to 4 marks. The Ganges is regarded as the goddess Ganga Mata; bathing in it purifies karma and brings spiritual blessings (1 mark). The Rig Veda 10.75 (Nadi-Stuti) praises the sacred rivers as sources of divine blessing (1 mark). The city of Varanasi on the Ganges is the holiest pilgrimage site — dying there is believed to grant moksha (1 mark). Many Hindus scatter the ashes of the dead in the Ganges to help the atman on its way to moksha (1 mark).
